How to build a simple wardrobe
that always looks good
Start with neutral colours. Navy, grey, white, black, olive. Everything matches everything, so getting dressed takes seconds and always looks put together.
Own a few great basics. Plain t-shirts, a white shirt, dark jeans, chinos. Simple pieces that fit well beat trendy pieces that don't.
Invest in one good jacket. A wool coat for winter or a clean bomber for spring. Outerwear is what people see first and remember.
Keep two pairs of shoes in perfect shape. Clean white sneakers and leather boots or loafers cover almost every situation.
Before: I spent money on clothes to feel better. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I feel sharp without new things.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I spent money on clothes to feel better. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I feel sharp without new things.

slides.texte_overlay: Get things tailored. A small adjustment on sleeves or trousers makes cheap clothes look expensive. It costs little and changes a lot.
Give away what you haven't worn in a year. A smaller wardrobe is easier to manage and makes every piece you own feel like a good choice.
